title: When tuba faded and Hines's 1931 strings band
summary: The first band had two clarinets, two fiddles and cello, giving a chamber sound.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Who played what: early band size and instrumentation

blocks.x: Well, to go back several years, you said when you first went with Hines, you were doubling?
Uh-huh.
When did you drop tuba in Hines' band?
I don't remember. It just -- tuba just started fading out, with all the big bands, just started fading out tuba, and the bass player was just playing string bass.
Yeah. I thought it made a big difference in how --
Made a big difference.
In how the bands sounded, how they swung. Earl didn't use a guitar, did he?
Yeah.
He did? Who was the guitar player?
Well, our first guitar player was Lawrence Dixon. He played guitar and cello.
Cello? Did he play any banjo?
Yeah, played banjo, too.
Played cello.
Yeah.
That's interesting.
Yeah, that first band we had was a great band, because we had two fiddles, we had Darnell Howard on fiddle, and Jimmy Mundy on fiddle, and we had Cecil Irwin on clarinet, and whatscallum on clarinet.
Omer Simeon?
Omer Simeon -- no, Omer Simeon -- yeah, Omer Simeon. So that give us two clarinets, two fiddles, and Lawrence Dixon doubled on cello. And me on string bass, that gives us a different sound.
Yeah, like a chamber group.
Yeah. So that's when we broke it up, when we went to New York.
Yeah?
Yeah, all them New York dudes just was talking and say how about that, you know, how about that. He doubles. He gets two phonic sound.
